name: Quillmetrics
label: Quillmetrics (product analytics)

planColumns.label: Integrations incl.
planColumns.help: How many destination tools (CRM, warehouse, messaging) the plan can sync to. Enterprise is unlimited, so a long tool list can push a scope up a tier.

planColumns.label: History (months)
planColumns.help: How far back analysts can query. Teams with year-over-year reporting need at least 12 months.

planColumns.label: SSO
planColumns.help: Whether SAML single sign-on is included. It's a common security requirement, so it often decides the tier on its own.

planColumns.label: Onboarding sessions
planColumns.help: Live sessions with a Quillmetrics analyst to set up dashboards for a team. When more teams need onboarding than the plan includes, the scope adds sessions.

planColumns.label: Price / 1k users / yr
planColumns.help: List price per 1,000 billable monthly tracked users per year. Leave it blank to hide pricing.

priceBooks.name: Illustrative list prices
priceBooks.note: Quillmetrics is fictional, and so are its prices.

params.label: Share of expected growth to pre-commit
params.help: How much of the customer's expected growth is built into the first-year commitment. 0.5 means half: a team expecting to double commits to 1.5× today's users.

params.label: Onboarding sessions per team
params.help: Live sessions each team needs to get its first dashboards running.

params.label: Extra onboarding rate ($/session)
params.title: Extra onboarding rate
params.help: Price for each onboarding session beyond what the plan includes. Leave it blank to show sessions without a price.

params.label: SE review above (thousand users)
params.title: Volume review threshold
params.help: Deals with more billable users than this go to a solutions engineer for custom volume pricing. 2000 means 2 million users.

params.label: Minimum weeks for 4+ integrations
params.help: Launching four or more integrations faster than this flags a timeline risk, so the rep can phase them.

questions.label: Monthly tracked users today
questions.buyerLabel: How many people use your product each month?

help.why: Billable usage starts here, so it sizes most of the deal.
help.listen: Seasonal peaks, a big launch coming, or free users who never log in.
help.ask: Is that monthly active users or total sign-ups? What does a peak month look like?
help.buyer: People who use your product at least once a month, in thousands. 250 means 250,000.

questions.label: Expected user growth, next 12 months
questions.buyerLabel: How fast do you expect to grow this year?

help.why: Part of expected growth is built into the commitment, so the customer isn't forced into an upgrade mid-term.
help.listen: Funding rounds, new markets, or a product launch.
help.ask: What's the growth target the board is holding you to?
help.buyer: We build some headroom into your plan so you don't have to renegotiate as you grow.

questions.label: Tools it needs to send data to
questions.buyerLabel: Which tools should your analytics connect to?

help.why: Each plan includes a set number of integrations, so a long list can move the tier.
help.listen: A data warehouse, a CRM the sales team lives in, or marketing automation.
help.ask: Which of these must be live on day one, and which can wait?
help.buyer: Pick the tools your teams already use. We sync your product data into them.

questions.label: How far back analysts need to query
questions.buyerLabel: How much history do you need to report on?

help.why: History allowances differ by plan and can force a higher tier.
help.listen: Year-over-year reporting, board decks, or seasonal comparisons.
help.ask: What's the oldest data someone asked for last quarter?
help.buyer: Year-over-year reporting needs at least 12 months.

questions.label: Teams who'll use it
questions.buyerLabel: How many teams will use dashboards?

help.why: Each team needs onboarding, which decides whether extra sessions are needed.
help.listen: Product, marketing, customer success, growth, or an exec team that wants its own view.
help.ask: Which team gets value first, and who's the internal champion for each?
help.buyer: For example product, marketing and customer success would be three teams.

help.why: SSO is only included from Scale up, so it often decides the plan by itself.
help.listen: Okta, Azure AD, an IT security questionnaire, or a recent audit.
help.ask: Does IT require SSO for every new tool, or only some?
help.buyer: Tick this if your IT team requires logins through Okta, Azure AD or similar.

help.why: HIPAA needs Enterprise; EU residency needs an SE to set up a regional workspace.
help.listen: Patient data, European customers, or a security review in progress.
help.ask: Who signs off on vendor security, and what's on their checklist?
help.buyer: Tell us now and your solutions engineer will bring the right documents to the first call.

help.why: Business-hours support starts at Growth; 24/7 needs Enterprise.
help.listen: Analytics shown to their own customers, or decisions made in real time.
help.ask: If dashboards were down for a day, who would notice first?
help.buyer: Choose 24/7 if your own customers see these numbers.

questions.label: Weeks to launch
questions.buyerLabel: When do you need it running?

help.why: Many integrations on a short timeline is where launches slip.
help.listen: A board meeting, a renewal, or a quarter-end deadline.
help.ask: What's driving the date, and which integration matters most for it?
help.buyer: Your target for the first dashboards in use.

rules.txt: Billable users = users today + a share of expected growth
Integrations needed > plan allowance → lowest plan that covers them
History needed > plan retention → lowest plan that keeps it
Onboarding needed > sessions included → add sessions
rules.msg: {teams} teams need about {sessions} onboarding sessions; {plan} includes {P.onboarding}. Add {sessGap} session{s(sessGap)}.

rules.txt: EU data residency → SE review (regional workspace)
rules.msg: EU data residency needs a dedicated EU workspace. Confirm region and pricing with a solutions engineer.

rules.txt: Billable users above threshold → SE review (volume pricing)
rules.msg: {fmtk(billable)} billable users is above the {fmtk(p.reviewUsers)} threshold. Route for custom volume pricing.

rules.txt: 4+ integrations on a short launch → timeline risk
rules.msg: {nDest} integrations in {launch} weeks; plan on {p.minLaunchWeeks}+. Launch the most important ones first and phase the rest.

rules.txt: Usage could double → suggest an annual true-up
rules.msg: Usage could double this year. An annual true-up avoids a mid-term upgrade.

checks.msg: No user count yet. Billable usage comes from monthly tracked users; confirm it with the prospect.

Security and compliance: {sso ? 'SAML single sign-on' : 'Email and password login'}{hipaa ? ', HIPAA BAA' : ''}{eu ? ', EU data residency' : ''}.
Questions leadership usually asks: what happens if users grow past the buffer, how pricing scales, and how fast teams see value. Your SE will answer these in the package.
terms: Someone who uses the customer's product at least once in a month. Quillmetrics is priced per 1,000 of them.
Users today plus a pre-committed share of expected growth.
Headroom built into the commitment so a growing customer isn't forced to upgrade mid-term.
A destination tool the data syncs to, such as a CRM, warehouse or messaging tool.
How many months back analysts can report on.
A live session with a Quillmetrics analyst to set up one team's dashboards.
Business Associate Agreement, the contract HIPAA requires before handling health data.
A flag that sends the scope to a solutions engineer before it's quoted.
faq: Why is billable usage higher than today's users?
Part of expected growth is built in, set by the growth buffer share on the Admin tab. It keeps a growing customer from hitting a mid-term upgrade.
Why did the plan jump to Enterprise?
Usually 24/7 support or HIPAA. Check Why this scope: each line names the rule and the answer that triggered it.
Each destination tool counts once, however much data goes to it.
No. It's a fictional sample catalog that shows ScopeOut running a second product with different questions, rules and plans, all loaded from one catalog file.

guide.ruleExample: Example: a team needs six integrations and single sign-on. Growth includes five integrations, so the integration rule requires Scale, and the SSO rule also requires Scale. The scope is Scale, and both reasons appear under Why this scope.
guide.ruleFlags: Some rules don't change the plan. They raise a flag instead: an onboarding gap, a tight launch, a deal large enough for SE review.
guide.estimateNote: Billable users = users today × (1 + expected growth × buffer share), rounded up. Onboarding sessions = teams × sessions per team.
guide.packagingNote: Plan allowances the engine scopes against. Quillmetrics is a fictional sample product, loaded from a catalog file to show ScopeOut adapting to a different business.
